name: all-2
statement: Most of the RL-Zero-Math gain is a saturating answer-mode switch: deliberate, then box the answer and stop, never the base's 'Answer:' line. The switch is encoded redundantly along one diffuse direction spread over every layer and matrix, so any unbiased fraction of the delta (half the matrices, a DARE 1 % sample, or a small multiple a of the whole delta) flips it. Accuracy is therefore a sharply concave function of delta scale; the cue flips the same switch from the prompt, and other RL runs (Code-RL) share part of it.
scope: Olmo-3-1025-7B base vs Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math (and the Code-RL delta from the same base), MATH-500 and the 328 harder problems, plain and cued prompts, T 0.6-1.0, weight interpolation and partial copies of the delta. It claims the switch explains the plain-base to RL gap up to about the cued-base level, not the last points past the cue (long-problem finishing), and it does not cover pass@k.

explains.quote: All MLP from RL alone 86.4; attention + norms alone 83.0
explains.how: Two disjoint halves of the delta each recover 75-85 % of the 34.8-point gain, a sub-additive pattern that a redundant, saturating switch produces.
A 0.1-3 % random sample of entries, rescaled, flips the switch as well as the whole MLP delta, despite 33-1,000x the noise energy.

explains.quote: Every arm that recovers accuracy also takes RL's format and length
explains.how: Accuracy and the answer-mode markers move together across arms, as expected if they are one switch.

explains.quote: D follows the answer format, not correctness
explains.how: The largest base-vs-RL log-probability differences sit on the answer-format token, not on correct-vs-wrong choices.
RL has driven the base's 'Answer:' mode to near zero probability, the clearest signature of the switch.
The cue adds nothing to RL because RL already sits in the mode the cue selects.
Two prompt tokens recover most of the RL gain, so most of the gain is a mode choice the base already has, not new skill.
The cue token appears in the late-MLP readouts of both RL deltas but not the SFT delta, so RL in general writes the same mode direction.
In another fine-tune pair the dose curve is concave and saturates below full scale, as a switch predicts.

explains.quote: closes 80-100 % of the gap on Math-500
explains.how: Label-free training recovers most of the MATH-500 gain, consistent with the gain being a mode that is easy to select rather than knowledge.

conflicts.how: Neuron contributions to KL add linearly, which a threshold-like switch would not obviously produce; the theory needs the saturation to occur between KL and accuracy, not in the distribution.
The Math-RL and Code-RL deltas are nearly orthogonal overall, so any shared switch component must be a small part of each.
A cued base already in the right mode still trails RL by 10 points, so the switch does not explain the last part of the gap.
Slips on RL-only items are not a format or mode effect.

rival: The gain is a linear accumulation of many small improvements (accuracy roughly proportional to delta scale, as the linear KL sum suggests). Separation: the rival predicts base + 0.25*(RL - base) on the plain prompt recovers about a quarter of the gain (about 284/500 at T 1.0) and that the cue still adds a lot at a = 0.5. This theory predicts about three quarters of the gain at a = 0.25 and almost no cue effect at a = 0.5.

predictions.experiment: base + 0.25*(RL - base), plain prompt, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, grader v3, MATH-500 one sample
base + 0.5*(RL - base), plain prompt, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, grader v3, MATH-500 one sample
base + 0.5*(RL - base) with the opening cue minus the same model with the plain prompt, T 1.0, MATH-500
predictions.refuted_by: the cue adds more than 20 items at a = 0.5

predictions.experiment: base + 1.0*(Code-RL - base) (Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Code final), plain prompt, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, grader v3, MATH-500 one sample
predictions.refuted_by: below 255 (no better than the plain base's 224 plus noise) or the share of answers with an 'Answer:' line stays at 35 % or more

predictions.experiment: Share of answers ending with an 'Answer:' line for base + 0.25*(RL - base), plain prompt, T 1.0, MATH-500
predictions.refuted_by: share at 30 % or more (the base arms' 41-46 %)
